saadway.description: SaadWay public dashboard RPC access. Principle V (constitution v1.2.0): the standalone dashboard is published to the LAN without a credential — its ubus calls are authorized as rpcd's default (unauthenticated) session. The compensating control is the platform's network boundary: the LAN-bound uhttpd listener (saadway/files/uci-defaults/40-saadway-uhttpd) and the firewall's WAN input policy. This group is attached to the 'saadway_login' login section (list read/write 'saadway'), i.e. it is the power set of an optional authenticated session.

unauthenticated.description: SaadWay standalone-dashboard access group (spec FR-020/FR-035, constitution v1.2.0, research.md D11). rpcd grants ONLY the group literally named 'unauthenticated' to its default session (openwrt/rpcd session.c:944-946 — a NULL login section), and the default session is the one an all-zero session id resolves to (include/rpcd/session.h:35 RPC_DEFAULT_SESSION_ID). uhttpd-mod-ubus checks every /ubus call through rpcd's session.access with the request's params[0] as the session id (openwrt/uhttpd ubus.c:280-297, 820-840) — so this group is what makes the dashboard's calls succeed without a session.login. It covers the 'saadway' ubus object only: no other ubus object is reachable by the dashboard. Residual risk: any host that can reach the LAN-bound listener can drive the whole saadway object — recorded in docs/verify-2512.md §7.
